_doc: The front lane's measures (2026-10-24): why the plate boundary and the subduction front are longer than Earth's. `front` splits the boundary into the plates' sizes (the sum of their spherical-cap perimeters) and their shapes (E, the sum of perimeters over the sum of cap perimeters), from the dynamics record alone; `boundgeom` measures the boundary's pieces between triple junctions, their tortuosity and the plates' perimeters with Bird 2003's own divider method, from the crust budget's maps (runs made with +DEEPTIME_CRUST_BUDGET_MAPS=@RUN@/maps). Pass it with --registry tools/review/pool/measures_front.json. Bird 2003's PB2002 numbers are tools/review/pool/bird/bird.py's over PB2002_plates.dig, PB2002_boundaries.dig and PB2002_steps.dat (the source library's Bird2003/, its output Bird2003/PB2002_geometry.json; ledger PLT-531). Definitions in measure_front.py and measure_boundgeom.py.

front.doc: the boundary as plate sizes times plate shapes, the front by the subducting plate's size and over time, and the shapes' excess by the plate's age, origin, speed guard, crust and speed; definitions in measure_front.py

boundgeom.doc: the boundary's pieces between triple junctions, their tortuosity, the plates' perimeters against spherical caps, the convergent front's runs and the plates' fragments, measured with Bird 2003's divider walks at 77 and 380 km on the visible samples' Delaunay triangulation, skipping the snapshots taken at a resampling; the _k7 columns put each map on one fixed lattice first (the model's samples sit on two lattices or more at a boundary, PB2002's raster on one); needs the crust budget's maps (+DEEPTIME_CRUST_BUDGET_MAPS=@RUN@/maps). The front is the boundary mix's subduction and collision fronts together (the maps' 256 and 512 flags since 2026-10-24; before, the TRENCH flag, which marked collisions' fronts too), so it reads against PB2002's SUB plus CCB, not SUB alone: Bird 2003 classes a continental convergent boundary (CCB, 23,003 km, unpolarised) apart from a subduction zone (SUB, 51,310 km) by the crust on both sides (Table 3, [127]), while the model's mix counts a front wherever an active contact converges, whatever the crust; front_sub is the like-for-like SUB column. Mallard et al. 2016 give Earth's trench length (48,000 km) as context. A like-for-like fix of the measure, not a moved target (plates.md, 'Step 7'; ledger PLT-531). The labels give PB2002 rasterised on the same 100,000-point lattice and put through the same code (tools/review/pool/bird/bird_raster.py), then Bird's own divider numbers; definitions in measure_boundgeom.py
